thread:
tess_customer: Hey team, after a traffic spike this morning our embeddings endpoint started returning intermittent 400s and a lot more ~1s tail latencies. Looks like the failures are 'dimension mismatch' errors. Happening across a few users. Anyone seen this with batching?

maria_support: Sorry about that — can you paste a couple of example requests/responses (scrub tokens) and the model name/variant you're hitting? Also which SDK and client batching options are you using?

ashish_eng_sre: tagging in SRE. If this is related to dynamic batching mixing model variants with different vector sizes we saw a regression in the runtime last quarter. Need logs + batch config.

kevin_runtime: Quick heads up — runtime should reject batches with mixed embedding dims, but there was a window where dynamic-shard batching could incorrectly merge shards if the routing table changed mid-batch. We'll want trace IDs.

ashish_eng_sre: @tess_customer can you share request trace id (x-request-id) or any traces from your side? Also what was max_batch_size + batch_window_ms in your client?

maria_support: If you don't have traces, a traffic log with timestamps + example client config will help reproduce.

Tess logs pasted: 

```
POST /v1/embeddings
model: text-embed-open-3b
client-config: {
  "max_batch_size": 128,
  "batch_window_ms": 20,
  "dynamic_batching": true
}
response sample error: {
  "error": "dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 768",
  "x-request-id": "r-20240315-9a7c"
}
```

maria_support: thanks. That error message is classic when two different model variants (or quantized vs float builds) with different embedding dims get batched together. Did you recently switch model alias to point to a new variant?

tess_customer: We did an internal canary last night switching alias from text-embed-open-3b-v1 to text-embed-open-3b-q4. Both were supposed to be 1536 but maybe one was an older 768 build? Not sure. Our deploys are frequent.

kevin_runtime: Can you run this curl on one of the failing request IDs and paste the full runtime debug header? `curl -I -H 'X-Request-Id: r-20240315-9a7c' https://api.redwood/trace` should return routing headers.

tess_customer: ran it, got: 
```
X-Serving-Model: text-embed-open-3b-q4
X-Model-Dim: 768
X-Serving-Node: gpu-32-xx
X-Batch-Id: b-20240315-551
X-Batch-Size: 12
```

ashish_eng_sre: aha. That confirms the variant returning 768 vectors. The alias may have pointed to mixed variants during the canary window. Dynamic batching then grouped requests destined for different model variants into a single batch which caused the mismatch.

maria_support: For immediate mitigation: 1) set client max_batch_size=1 or disable dynamic_batching to avoid cross-shard mixing; 2) pin the model variant (use model: text-embed-open-3b-q4) until we stabilize; 3) we'll add a gateway-side check to reject mixed-dim batches with a clearer error and early rejection rather than returning partial 400s.

kevin_runtime: Follow-up: runtime team will push a hotfix to validate dims at batch-assemble time. Patch will: 
- annotate each request with declared "vector_size" at ingress
- verify all requests in a batch have same "vector_size" before KV-cache/concat
- if mismatch, return a 409 with structured error: {"code":"BATCH_DIM_MISMATCH","expected":1536,"found":768}
This should prevent silent downstream failures.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime/validate-batch-dims hotfix -> canary 2 nodes (eta 18m).

ashish_eng_sre: For the observed tail latency spike: when dynamic batching mixes shards we can get head-of-line blocking and backpressure — some requests block waiting for KV/cache layout compatibility. Two levers: reduce batch_window_ms (lower tail but higher efficiency tradeoff) or decrease max_batch_size. For now, lowering max_batch_size to 32 and batch_window_ms to 10ms is a good compromise.

tess_customer: We're willing to try that. Any guidance on the perf hit?

maria_support: Expect ~5-15% cost increase if you halve batch efficiency, but tail p95 latency should drop from ~1.0s to ~200-400ms depending on traffic shape.

kevin_runtime: Also check if your SDK set `batch_by_model_alias=true`. If alias routing is enabled, it can cause per-request routing changes that interact badly with dynamic batching. If you pin variant directly we avoid alias ambiguity.

tess_customer: Changing client config now and pinning variant. Will report back in ~10m.

(12 minutes later)

tess_customer: Update: after setting `max_batch_size=32` and pinning to text-embed-open-3b-q4 tail latency p95 dropped to ~320ms and errors stopped. Thanks.

maria_support: Great. We'll keep the incident open until runtime hotfix is live. Kevin/Ashish — any postmortem action items?

kevin_runtime: Action items: 1) land and rollout validate-batch-dims hotfix (PR #4212), 2) add server-side metric `batch_dim_mismatch_count` and an alert at >1/min, 3) document best practices in support KB (pin variants during canaries, recommended batching defaults), 4) add SDK change to prefer model pinning when dynamic_batching is true.

ashish_eng_sre: I'll add a temporary alert to catch spikes and correlate with alias switch events.

maria_support: Noted. @tess_customer I'll follow up by email with a short repro checklist and recommended client config. Feel free to re-open if you see anything else. :thumbsup:

tess_customer: Appreciate it, team.

kevin_runtime: deploy-bot: runtime/validate-batch-dims canary success on 2 nodes. scheduling full rollout now.

deploy-bot: rollout complete: runtime/validate-batch-dims -> stable (2024-03-15T14:48:00Z).

maria_support: closing the thread for now. If the customer sees the issue again we'll reopen and escalate to SEs.

(End of thread)
